full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Abdur Rashid, J. : The above rule was obtained by the pre-emptors upon an application under Section-115 of the Code of Civil Procedure made against the judgment and order dated 16.06.85 passed by Subordinate Judge at Rajshahi in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 58 of 1983 setting aside those dated 27.06.83 passed by Sadar Munsif at Rajshahi in Miscellaneous Case No. 265 of 1977 under Section-96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 7. I have perused the judgment of the trial court as well as that of the appellate court and also the application under Section-115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. I have, also examined the evidence, oral and documentary on record. It is not disputed that opposite party No. 1 is a stranger to the holding. Opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 transferred 181 shatak out of 53 shatak of land of plot No. 443 appertaining to khatian No. 705 to opposite party No. 1 by a deed of sale executed on 20.03.73. The sale deed was duly registered on 13.07.77 the application under Section-96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption was made on 14.09.77. The petitioners are co-sharers in the holding. So their application for pre-emption was rightly held by the trial court not barred by limitation. They are also entitled to get the land pre-empted as the petitioners had 8/10 bighas of land only in total.
